- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: POWERING UP AGAIN - Western schools looking towards solar installations post-Melissa.
WESTERN BUREAU: At least two western Jamaica high schools that were damaged during Hurricane Melissa last October are looking to expand the solar-power facilities they had prior to the category-5 hurricane as a means of providing long-term renewable energy to power their operations. Muschett High School in Wakefield, Trelawny, and Herbert Morrison Technical High in Montego Bay, St James, were among hundreds schools pounded by the hurricane on October 28 last year. It wrecked the small solar-power infrastructure they had in place at the time.

South Asia - bottom line: CM Afridi strikes defiant tone as federal ministers rail against KP govt's counter-terror fight.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: CM Afridi strikes defiant tone as federal ministers rail against KP govt's counter-terror fight.
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday struck a defiant tone and again panned the Centre’s counterterrorism policy as federal ministers railed against his government’s efforts to combat terrorism. Afridi, who was elected as the KP CM in October 2025, has repeatedly voiced his opposition to the federal government’s policies on counterterrorism and Afghanistan.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Al Jazeera - Middle East, The Hindu - International, one hour ago: 5 men held over bomb scare at England base used by US to attack Iran are UK nationals: police.
Five men held over a bomb scare at a British air base used by the US are all UK nationals aged in their mid-20s, British counter-terror police said Monday. The five — a 25-year-old, three men aged 24 and a 23-year-old — all based in London, have been detained since Sunday on suspicion of offences including “preparation of a terrorist act” under UK anti-terrorism laws, according to police. The five were questioned by the police on Monday.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: CM Afridi wants KP input included in counterterror policy.
KP CM Sohail Afridi and his predecessor, Ali Amin Gandapur, inquire after those injured in the Darazinda attack.—Dawn DERA ISMAIL KHAN: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Sunday called for better cooperation between the provincial and federal governments on security matters, saying the counterterrorism policy should reflect ground realities. The chief minister made these comments during his visit to Dera Ismail Khan to visit the wounded, a day after a deadly bombing targeting a police and customs check-post killed more than 12 people, including rescue officials, in Darazinda.
